column2: Δx · Δp ≥ ħ/2, where Δx is the uncertainty in position, Δp is the uncertainty in momentum, and ħ is the reduced Planck constant. It means that the more precisely the position of a particle is determined, the less precisely its momentum can be known, and vice versa.

column2: iħ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ, where i is the imaginary unit, ħ is the reduced Planck constant, ψ is the wave function, and Ĥ is the Hamiltonian operator.
